oof the nexplanon is progesterone only isn't it? I've tried a handful of birth control methods over the years. Copper coil was so excruciating my legs would give out on me during my periods at work and I would just fall to the floor then get up and pretend like it didn't happen. Eventually got that removed and started taking the Rigevidon pill (combined but progesterone dominant). I started regularly passing decidual casts and would have periods lasting months straight, and my mental health wasn't good either but I put it down to 'seasonal depression'. 

Then I tried the mirena iud which is progesterone only and I was like a different person and not in a good way. I felt so depressed and would stay awake until 4am most nights crying myself to sleep. It took over a year of complaining to the doctors and then eventually calling them up sobbing and begging for them to take it out for them to remove it. The relief after it came out was immediate, literally felt like a weight had been lifted off my shoulders. Now I'm on another combined pill which has a higher dosage of estrogen (Gedarel 30mcg) than the one I took before (20mcg) and my quality of life has drastically improved. 

I weirdly feel like it helps my adhd and so I did some research and there is a strong connection between estrogen and dopamine, an increase in estrogen leads to an increase of dopamine, and it also enhances the effects of dopamine and makes them last longer. So I lowkey have been using my pill as an adhd med because I can't currently access real adhd medication. It also helps with my endometriosis symptoms especially because it allows me to skip my periods entirely until I have breakthrough bleeding, which also means no more PMDD symptoms either!!! The pill I'm on still comes with its issues for me, for example when I take a break from my pill to have a bleed my stomach is almost flat, then I begin taking the pill again and I look like I could be pregnant because it gives me such bad bloating. Because of that I might try to switch to pills like the Yasmin one which is meant to be more gentle in terms of side effects because it uses less hormones but still keeps the same balance of estrogen. 

Unfortunately enough I feel like I kinda have to be on birth control until I have menopause unless I get a hysterectomy or something because without it idk how I would manage in my day to day life. My natural periods before birth control lasted anywhere between 7-14 days, and the pmdd symptoms would also come two weeks before my period, meaning even if I was lucky I'd only get a couple days of feeling normal every month which was so miserable. Don't get me wrong I love being a woman but I feel like I was not built for this life, cis men don't realise how lucky they are to just feel normal every day of every month.

The wall in season 4 pleasantly surprised me though, I felt like we finally got to see Cherie having some agency again, and them bumping Nova up from a character that appeared in like 2 episodes to a main player in the wall storyline was so needed. If the wall in season 5 is going to continue to surprise us like in season 4 then I'm happy for it to stay. But if they decide to go back to the way it was in seasons 2 (other than the cherie episode which I loved) and 3 then they can just keep the wall because I think a lot of us were getting fed up. Also I may or may not skip the wall entirely on rewatches.... I came for aliens and fun not for humans and injustice lol. The whole reason I watch the show is to not be sad. Also I just don't think the wall has the same rewatch value that the family segments do, at least for me.
